 Travel disrupted and events cancelled as Storm Boelo hits UK with wind and rain
24 October 2026
 Summary
 This live page is now closed, but you can read more in our news story 
 Storm Boelo is bringing more wet and windy weather to large parts of the UK - a day after Storm Austen hit the country 
 Ferries in the Irish Sea are cancelled, some Scottish rail lines will close from 21:00, while in Ireland, some flights to and from Dublin were cancelled - here's a travel round-up 
 Meanwhile, a marathon in the Eryri national park in north Wales was called off, as well as a range of events in England, Scotland , and Northern Ireland 
 One couple , stuck in Guernsey, tell us "it's been incredibly stressful" after their flight home to Gatwick airport was cancelled
 The Met Office has issued six weather warnings covering much of the UK between Saturday and Sunday - three are already in effect , while amber warnings for wind begin at 21:00
 This satellite image , shared by the weather agency, shows Storm Boelo as seen from space
 Thousands of homes are still without power following Friday's storm, according to the National Grid

 Live Reporting
 Edited by Charlotte Hadfield
 Second storm in two days brings travel disruption across UK published at 18:16 BST 18:16 BST 
 Katie Williams 
Live reporter 
 Image source, Getty Images 
 The second storm in two days has brought wet and windy weather to the UK, causing travel disruption and event cancellations.
 Scotland, Northern Ireland and the north of England are bracing for the worst of Storm Boelo, with gusts of up to 80mph forecast.
 Three yellow weather warnings are already in place for wind and rain, impacting areas from Scotland right down to southern England. 
 Another three warnings will kick in this evening from 21:00, including two more serious amber warnings for wind impacting Northern Ireland, Scotland and northern England. We've got full details on those here. 
 Halloween events have been cancelled in Scotland and Northern Ireland, a marathon has been called off in North Wales and Knowsley Safari Park in Merseyside, north-west England, will be closed tomorrow. 
 National Rail has announced disruption on a number of lines, flights to and from Dublin Airport have been cancelled, and highway authorities are urging drivers to take particular care and avoid non-essential journeys.
 A number of power cuts in the Glasgow and Edinburgh areas have already been reported to SP Energy Networks, while power outages continue to affect large parts of south-west England following Friday's Storm Austen.
 We're pausing our live coverage now, but you can read the latest in our news story.

 Could we see three storms in a row? published at 17:53 BST 17:53 BST 
 Matt Taylor 
BBC Weather 
 Storm Boelo follows hot on the heels of Storm Austen, but forecasts also show the potential for yet another deep area of low pressure to arrive later on Monday and into Tuesday. 
 It's too early to say if this one will be named, but it looks likely to follow a similar track to Boelo, with the strongest winds focused towards the north of the UK.
 A succession of storms is perhaps not as unusual as you think. 
 When you have a strong jet stream roaring across the Atlantic as we do right now, areas of low pressure can easily be developed and steered towards the UK in quick succession. 
 In February 2022 three named storms had big impacts in Northern Ireland - Eunice, Dudley and Franklin.
 A fourth storm is looking unlikely though as our weather quietens down through the week.
 Image source, PA

 Cornish cafe serving free hot drinks to people hit by power cuts published at 17:36 BST 17:36 BST 
 Caroline Robinson 
South West 
 The Arborist cafe, just outside of Truro in Cornwall, has been welcoming people who do not have power in their homes.
 "We do this for the storms now, we did it in Storm Goretti," says co-owner Louise Martin. 
 "You can help yourself to tea and coffee, bring a book, we've got games here...and you can charge your phones and devices, and if you want, bring flasks and things to fill up with hot water."
 Cafe visitor Julie Le Masurier describes it as a "brilliant surprise" and a "lovely, lovely thing to do for the community".
 Her and Andrew Le Masurier say they have been without power since early Friday morning and are not expecting it to be back on until Sunday.

 Winds continue to strenghten as gusts of 76mph recorded published at 17:26 BST 17:26 BST 
 The winds are continuing to strengthen as Storm Boelo takes hold. 
 Here are the strongest gusts recorded around the UK so far on Saturday, as recorded in miles per hour:
 South Uist - 76mph (122.31 km/h)
 Inverbervie - 71
 Aberdaron - 68
 Tiree - 68
 Capel Curig - 68
 Magilligan - 66
 Altnaharra - 64
 Stornoway - 64
 Killowen - 63
 Pembrey Sands - 62
 Salsburgh - 62
 Valley - 61
 Dundrennan - 60
 St Mary's, Scilly - 60

 Events cancelled this weekend as strong winds hit UK published at 17:17 BST 17:17 BST 
 Image source, EPA/Shutterstock 
 Storm Boelo has caused a number of closures and cancellations at events and attractions across the country this weekend. Here are some of them:
 In Merseyside, Liverpool City Council has confirmed Saturday's River of Light event is cancelled for the second night in a row due to safety
 Knowsley Safari Park has also announced the site will be closed on Sunday 25 October "due to high winds"
 Several markets across the North West have also been cancelled due to the weather, including Quayside Makers Market in Salford on Sunday, and Macclesfield Treacle Market in Cheshire
 Meanwhile Northamptonshire Day in Kettering , which celebrates the county's heritage, has been postponed on Sunday due to the forecast conditions
 In Scotland, Paisley's popular Halloween festival has also fallen foul of the weather
 A Halloween family fun day at Dean Park Castle and Country Park in Kilmarnock, scheduled for Sunday, has been postponed

 Storm Boelo to bring severe gales and heavy rain to parts of UK published at 16:54 BST 16:54 BST 
 Storm Boelo is likely to cause damage and disruption as we move through tonight and into Sunday as the winds continue to strengthen, according to BBC Weather's Stav Danaos.
 You can watch the full forecast in the video below.

 Dublin Airport cancels flights and warns of further disruption published at 16:40 BST 16:40 BST 
 Storm Boelo is continuing to cause travel disruption this afternoon.
 In Ireland, Dublin Airport has announced that as of 16:00, nine outbound flights and 10 inbound flights have been cancelled due to weather issues.
 Meanwhile, six flights carried out a go-around procedure after being unable to land, with five landing on the second attempt, according to the airport.
 It adds that the other flight was forced to divert to another airport before returning a short time later.
 "Winds are forecast to remain strong for the rest of the day, which may lead to further disruption," the airport says on X, adding that passengers should travel to the airport as normal and monitor their airline for updates.
 Image source, PA 
 Image caption, Storm Boelo brings wind and rain to Carlingford, Ireland

 New flood warnings for Cumbria, Greater Manchester and Merseyside published at 16:23 BST 16:23 BST 
 Image source, EPA/Shutterstock 
 Image caption, New Brighton, Merseyside, is among the areas covered by flood warnings
 New flood warnings and alerts have been issued since this morning. 
 There are now six warnings in place, indicating flooding is expected, and 39 alerts , indicating it is possible. A warning is the more serious of the two categorisations. 
 The warnings cover: 
 Cumbrian coastline from Gretna to Silloth including Port Carlisle, Skinburness and Rockcliffe
 Cumbrian coastline from Silloth to St Bees, between Allonby and Whitehaven
 Cumbrian coastline from Silloth to St Bees including Maryport, Flimby, Workington and Whitehaven
 Cumbrian coastline from St Bees Head to Haverigg, along the coast from North Head to Haverigg
 Irish Sea at New Brighton in Merseyside
 Lee's Bridge at Astley Bridge Central, Bolton, Greater Manchester
 People in these areas are encouraged to avoid seafronts and harbours, as well as coastal roads, footpaths and carparks which may be flooded.
 The three warnings we reported earlier have now been lifted.

 This satellite image, issued by the Met Office, shows Storm Boelo as seen from space, covering the UK.
 The weather agency has issued a number of yellow and amber warnings for wind and rain across the country on Saturday and Sunday. You can read more on these warnings in our earlier post.

 Northern half of UK expected to be worst affected by Storm Boelo published at 15:52 BST 15:52 BST 
 Annie Flury 
BBC News 
 Strong winds and heavy rain are forecast to continue across the UK
over the weekend as Storm Boelo moves eastwards, bringing the risk of travel
disruption, power cuts and localised flooding.
 The worst-affected areas are forecast to be across the northern
half of the UK. 
 The Met Office has issued an amber wind warning for much of
 Scotland and parts of northern England from 21:00 BST on Saturday to 21:00 on Sunday.
 In Northern Ireland , a second amber warning for wind runs across
parts of the north of the region from 21:00 on Saturday to 10:00 on
Sunday.
 While the worst of Saturday's weather is forecast to be felt in
areas covered by warnings, heavy and persistent rain is expected across larger
parts of the UK.
 Spray and surface water could make driving conditions hazardous,
while further downpours increase the risk of localised flooding.
 Strong winds are forecast to continue into Sunday, although rain
should gradually ease across most of the country.
 Sunny spells and blustery showers are expected elsewhere, while
 north-east Scotland is likely to see the most persistent rainfall.

 Locals come together to help after beach cafe closed by stormy weather published at 15:35 BST 15:35 BST 
 Oliver Slow 
BBC Wales News 
 Image source, Tafell a Tan 
 Locals have been helping out after a beach cafe in west Wales was
forced to close following winds from Storm Austen - which hit yesterday - left it covered in sand.
 The owners of Tafell a Tan in Llangrannog, Ceredigion, posted
pictures of the "sandstorm" on Friday. They later showed people coming out to help the clean-up, including using a digger.
 "Llangrannog at its absolute finest, thank you great people," they
said.

 Trains, roads and ferries disrupted by Storm Boelo published at 15:19 BST 15:19 BST 
 Image source, Getty Images 
 Trains 
 TransPennine Express is encouraging essential travel only on Saturday and Sunday
 Avanti West Coast is advising people to avoid travelling north of Preston on Sunday
 LNER is advising people not to travel between Edinburgh and Aberdeen on Sunday
 There are also service alterations on CrossCountry, Great Western Railway, Northern, ScotRail and Transport for Wales
 Roads 
 National Highways - which manages motorways and some A roads in England - has issued an amber warning for the north east and north west from midnight tonight until 16:00 tomorrow. It urges people to take extra care due to the risk of falling branches and wind-blown debris
 Meanwhile, the police in Scotland have warned of "hazardous" conditions and a high risk of disruption on the road network
 Traffic Wales is warning that high winds could result in restrictions in some places, including on the A55 Britannia Bridge. It is also warning of "poor driving conditions" on sections of the M4 due to high winds
 In Londonderry , Foyle Bridge will remain closed until further notice due to high winds, while police in Northern Ireland are advising drivers that traffic disruption is possible
 Ferries 
 Providers such as StenaLine, Irish Ferries and P&O Ferries have also cancelled a number of ferry crossings in the Irish Sea
 Image source, PA

 National Grid: 6,075 properties still without power in south-west published at 15:07 BST 15:07 BST 
 We can now bring you a more exact figure following our earlier post on power cuts . 
 National Grid figures show a total of 6,075 properties are still without power in south-west England at the time of writing. 
 As a reminder, the distributer says over 117,000 properties have had their power restored since the start of the storm.

 'It's incredibly stressful': Couple stuck in Guernsey after multiple flights cancelled published at 14:57 BST 14:57 BST 
 Bernadette McCague 
Your Voice 
 Sue Fairbrother and her husband Rob are stuck in Guernsey after their flight home to Gatwick airport was cancelled on Thursday.
 The couple say they have missed their grandchild's birthday party after being faced with another cancellation yesterday, and they are now waiting for a flight home on Sunday.
 "It has been incredibly stressful not knowing if our next flight is being cancelled without warning and then [being] given a random flight days in advance", Sue tells the BBC.
 "We have missed our grandchild’s birthday party and numerous other appointments", Sue says, adding that she is "constantly checking the flight website to see if they have cancelled us again”.

 Image source, PA Media 
 As we've been reporting, there are yellow warnings in place for wind and rain across much of the UK - with more severe amber warnings due to begin in northern areas at 21:00 BST.
 None of the warnings cover London - but that doesn't mean it's ice cream weather in the capital, as these pictures show...

 Red marine warning issued as Dublin airport cancels flights published at 14:32 BST 14:32 BST 
 Adam Mandeville 
BBC News NI 
 A status red marine warning has been issued for parts of the island of Ireland’s coast by Irish meteorological service Met Éireann.
 The warning covers Rossan Point to Bloody Foreland to Fair Head – all on the north coast of the island of Ireland.
 Met Éireann says winds in these areas will reach violent storm force 11 at times.
 Meanwhile, Dublin Airport says that, as of 12:00 local time, five outbound and four inbound flights have been “cancelled by airlines due to weather issues”.
 They adds that “winds are forecast to increase as the day goes on, which may lead to some further disruption”.
 Image source, Met Éireann

 Thousands of properties still without power in aftermath of Storm Austen published at 14:08 BST 14:08 BST 
 A map from National Grid shows thousands of homes and businesses are still without power after Storm Austen battered parts of the country yesterday.
 The south-west of England in particular is still experiencing large clusters of power cuts. This includes: 141 properties without power near Beaminster in Dorset, 384 without power near Whimple in East Devon, and 168 hit by power cuts near Penhale in Cornwall. 
 National Grid says 117,320 properties have been restored with power supplies since the beginning of the storm. 
 Image source, National Grid

 Some Scottish rail lines to close ahead of amber wind warning published at 13:42 BST 13:42 BST 
 Catherine Lyst 
BBC Scotland 
 Network Rail has confirmed that a number of routes will close as a precaution, while speed restrictions will be introduced across much of Scotland's railways.
 As a reminder: The Met Office has issued an amber warning for wind over Scotland and northern England from 21:00 on Saturday to 21:00 on Sunday. 
 The following rail line closures are planned:
 • Glasgow Central – Ayr will close between Kilwinning and Ayr from 21:00 on Saturday. After 21:00, a half hourly shuttle service will operate between Glasgow Central and Kilwinning in both directions
 • Glasgow Queen Street – Oban / Mallaig will close between Fort William and Mallaig and between Crianlarich and Oban from about 22:00 on Saturday
 • Inverness – Kyle of Lochalsh will close between Kyle of Lochalsh and Achnashellach from the start of service on Sunday
 • Inverness – Wick / Thurso will close between Helmsdale and Wick / Thurso from the start of service on Sunday
 Image source, Met Office

 Foyle Bridge shut down due to high winds in Northern Ireland published at 13:28 BST 13:28 BST 
 Adam Mandeville 
BBC News NI 
 Image source, Getty Images 
 Police in Northern Ireland are advising drivers that traffic disruption is possible due to the weather conditions.
 They also advise motorists to “take extra care” if they must travel and to reduce their speed “because of the possibility of surface water” and to avoid driving through flood water.
 “It may be necessary to close some roads or put temporary restrictions in place - road users are reminded to adhere to road signs and any temporary traffic lights,” a police statement says.
 The storm has also caused a number of road closures in the Republic of Ireland.
 Meanwhile, in Londonderry, Foyle Bridge will remain closed until further notice due to high winds.

 South Uist - 72mph (115 km/h)
 Tiree - 68mph

 Aberdaron - 59mph
 Islay / Port Ellen - 58mph
 Capel Curig - 57mph
 Needles - 56mph
